one_liner: A DoD analyst who plans and oversees IT contracts for DMDC, acting as Contracting Officer's Representative and handling acquisition documents, milestones, and budgets.
fit_summary: This role requires a year of GS-11-level IT acquisition work: drafting statements of work, market research and cost estimates, supporting pre- and post-award contract functions and tracking IT budgets. Daniel's market research and proposal work at IEM was contractor-side and not IT acquisition, so he likely won't qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and military spouses under Direct Hire Authority, so no federal status is needed and traditional rating and ranking does not apply.

GS-12 requires one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-11 in IT acquisition planning, pre-/post-award contract support, acquisition documents (market research, SOWs, cost estimates), milestone tracking, and IT budget execution.
GS-13 requires one year at the GS-12 equivalent: independently authoring Acquisition Strategies, PWS, and IGCEs, managing the full post-award lifecycle, and formulating multi-year IT budgets.
Education cannot substitute for specialized experience at either grade.
You must be able to obtain and keep a Secret clearance.
strategy: Apply only if he can document about a year of contract tasks at GS-11 level; his contractor-side proposal work and spending reports are the closest, and HR may not count them.

Describe contractor-side work accurately: market research on SAM.gov, GovWin and DHS forecasts, and leading proposal writing for federal contracts (2019 to 2024). His resume doesn't show cost estimates or task-order tracking, so claim them only if he did them.
Stay within the two-page limit by listing exact dates, hours per week, and title for each job, and by keeping emergency-management content that isn't about acquisition to one line.

The posting is open until 2026-11-15, but direct-hire postings can close early or pull applicants in batches, so apply early. Meanwhile, consider taking a free FAI/DAU COR course (CLC 106) to build credibility.

If you don't qualify, focus instead on GS-0301/0343 emergency-management or policy roles at FEMA, Virginia VDEM, or Prince William County emergency management, which match your background much better.
resume_bullets: Procured and tracked medical supplies for COVID-19 sites, with pivot-table reports on spending and order status (2021–2022).
Found federal opportunities in SAM.gov and GovWin and led proposal writing (2019–2024).
interview_questions: Walk us through your experience with pre-award acquisition documents such as SOWs, PWS, or IGCEs.
How would you oversee contractor performance as a COR when a vendor misses a deliverable?
Describe how you have tracked or executed a budget, including which fund types or appropriations you worked with.
Give an example of a process you mapped and improved.
watch_outs: Without documented IT acquisition and contract experience, you will likely be rated ineligible, since education cannot substitute for experience.
A Secret clearance is required, so expect a background investigation.
Location is listed as multiple and remote work is not allowed, so confirm a duty station within commuting distance of Manassas (DMDC has locations such as Alexandria and Seaside, CA).
